# Handoff: printer and filament calibration in JusPrin

Written 2026-10-21, revised 2026-10-22 for the one-popup flow, for the agent who implements calibration. Nothing is
coded yet; this document records the decisions Kenneth made, the facts verified in OrcaSlicer's code (by reading and,
for the flow, by running), the design on the canvas, and the smallest build that satisfies both. Read
`agent-docs/jusprin/README.md` and the documents it lists first; `fork-stewardship.md` governs every line you change
outside `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`. This file is untracked on purpose: never commit it.

## 1. What a calibration is, in one paragraph

A person has a symptom (stringing, under-extrusion, bulging corners) or just wants a filament dialled in. One popup
tells them their project will be saved and closed; then they are in an empty calibration project of its own, whose
agent has the context handed over, picks the test with them (asking only when the symptom did not decide it), and
generates OrcaSlicer's own test geometry into that project. The person prints it and sends a photo, the agent reads
the print, and the result is saved as a new preset whose name the person is told to use from now on. The product
definition's section 2.11 lists the eight agent steps; this handoff is how they map onto code.

## 2. Decisions already made (Kenneth, 2026-10-21 and 2026-10-22)

1. A calibration is a project of its own, as long as the person is told what will happen before their project is
   closed. Not a plate in the current project (see fact 1 below for why that is impossible without rewriting Orca).
2. First batch: temperature tower, flow rate, pressure advance. Nothing else in this iteration.
3. The outcome of every test is a new preset: a named copy of the filament (or of the process or printer preset for
   the tests that write there). The app does not switch any project to it. The receipt names the preset and the
   agent tells the person to pick it from now on.
4. No remembered "return to the previous project". The test project is left through Home like any project.
5. No per-test UI. Adding a test must be a declaration plus skill text, not page code.
6. The physical-print ledger: "doesn't matter, whatever is the easiest". Leave it alone.
7. Entry points are hard-coded: a "Calibrate…" row in the project header's printer chip menu, in the filament slot
   menu, and in the Home printer card's kebab. A symptom typed in the project chat leads to the same flow.
8. The confirmation before a calibration is the Agent page's own Confirmation dialog, the one it draws for "Delete
   chat?": a web dialog, not Orca's `MessageDialog` and not a new native dialog (2026-10-21).
9. **One popup, then the calibration project** (2026-10-22, confirmed after the verification in fact 9). The popup
   names the filament and printer, not a test. After it, JusPrin creates and opens an empty, named calibration project
   and its chat, with the context handed over. The agent in that chat picks the test, asking "which test?" only when
   the handover does not decide it, and generates into that same project. The first implementation's flow (a popup
   about closing the project, then the agent asking which test, then a second project) is what this replaces.
10. Home's project cards do not change: no slice state, filament or calibration result on a card. The test is told
    apart by its project name (2026-10-22).
11. Choices under the agent's words are Chat/Reply Choice chips, never buttons. Buttons inside the thread belong only
    to cards drawn from tool results, the proposal and the receipt (2026-10-22).

## 3. Facts verified in the code

Facts 1 to 8 were verified by reading on 2026-10-21; fact 9 by running code on 2026-10-22.

1. **Every OrcaSlicer generator replaces the open project and edits project-wide presets.** `Plater::calib_pa`,
   `calib_temp`, `calib_flowrate`, `calib_max_vol_speed`, `calib_retraction`, `calib_VFA`, the input-shaping pair and
   `Calib_Cornering` (`src/slic3r/GUI/Plater.cpp` from about line 12677) each call `new_project()` and then write to
   `preset_bundle->prints/filaments/printers.get_edited_preset().config`. Plates have no presets of their own, so a
   test on a plate of an existing project would change every other plate. Do not try.
2. **The test's parameters are runtime-only.** The generator stores them on the current plate's `Print` with
   `set_calib_params` (`Print.hpp:1089`); `GCode.cpp` reads them per layer (temperature at line 4697). Nothing writes
   them to the 3MF, and loading a project resets the mode to none at `Plater.cpp:5891`. A saved temperature tower,
   reopened, slices as a plain tower at one temperature. The pressure-advance pattern is the exception: its per-layer
   commands go into the plate's custom G-code, which the 3MF does save. The PA pattern also hard-codes the first
   plate's origin (`Plater.cpp:12814`), which is right because the generator's `new_project()` selects plate 0.
3. **OrcaSlicer already treats one outcome as a new preset.** The Bambu wizard's save page writes flow results as a
   filament preset named "<filament> Flow Rate Calibrated" (`CalibrationWizardSavePage.cpp:37`). Its pressure-advance
   results go to the machine, not a preset. The SoftFever dialogs (`calib_dlg.cpp`) save nothing: the person types
   the value into a preset by hand.
4. **Saving a copy already exists and selects the copy.** `settings_apply_patch` with `persistAs` saves through
   Orca's own `Tab::save_preset` and asserts the copy is now selected
   (`Workspace/OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:3356-3369`); the result carries `saved_as`. A stock preset cannot be
   overwritten and the preview says so with `read_only_preset` and a suggested copy name (`check_persist`, line
   2941). Whether a process-scope copy works end to end is unverified; filament and printer are in use today.
5. **Which preset each result belongs to** (from `Preset.cpp`'s option lists): nozzle temperature, flow ratio,
   pressure advance, retraction length (as a filament override) and max volumetric speed are filament settings; VFA
   writes wall speeds in the process preset; cornering writes junction deviation (process) or jerk limits (printer);
   input shaping and Bambu's measured pressure advance live on the machine and produce no preset.
6. **The skill mechanism is ready.** `AgentUI/src/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` with a `description:` in its frontmatter is
   listed to the model and read on demand through the `skill_read` tool (`Agent/ToolRegistry.cpp:1209`,
   `AgentHost.cpp:2467`); a skill may also carry a `trigger:` the app fires on an event (`skillParser.ts`). Text limit
   16 KiB; one skill per directory; name equals directory name.
7. **The project-replacing path already exists.** The `project_open` tool saves the open project to its version
   history, drops unsaved preset edits, and calls `m_plater.new_project(true, true, name)` with confirmations skipped
   (`OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:2450-2467`, `ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp:1005`). Creating the calibration project
   takes this route, not a second one.
8. **The setup card is already data-driven.** `setup_record` (`ToolRegistry.cpp:1071`) titles the pinned card from a
   purpose and headline. A calibration project needs no new pinned card: the agent records the test as the purpose
   and the range as the headline.
9. **Generating into a project JusPrin already opened, verified by running** (report:
   `.claude/worktrees/kind-mestorf-a37ba6/calibration-generate-verification.md`, untracked; its probe, harness diff
   and log are in the shared notes folder `calibration-generate-probe/`). With the real adapter and shell, each of
   the three generators called in a fresh, empty, named JusPrin project:
   - shows no dialog, and builds a test identical to OrcaSlicer's own dialog path: same objects on plate 0, same
     per-object settings, same `calib_params` on the plate's print, same preset edits, and for the PA pattern the
     same per-layer custom G-code after `reslice()`;
   - but replaces the project all the same: the JusPrin project id, the workspace session and the chat document
     change, because `new_project()` gives the model a new auxiliary directory and `ProjectPersistence` treats that
     as a project boundary (`ProjectPersistence.cpp:181-185`, `start_fresh_identity`). An empty project that already
     holds a chat is saved by the shell's release hook and appears on Home as a separate project;
   - renames the project; `Plater::set_project_filename(name)` restores JusPrin's name, and the name survives a save
     only if it is set before the first autosave (`ProjectAutosave.cpp:515-519` fixes the name at the first version);
   - keeps an unsaved preset edit made in the empty project: it carries into the test, because JusPrin's release hook
     skips OrcaSlicer's keep-or-discard question (`Plater.cpp:12077`).
   So the one-popup flow needs the carry-over in 5.1 and no change to OrcaSlicer-owned code. The report recommends
   against a seam that lets a generator skip its own `new_project()`: three functions in `Plater.cpp`, and it would
   skip resets that keep the test identical to OrcaSlicer's.

## 4. The design

JusPrin v2 canvas, page "Calibration · Printer & Filament": https://claude.ai/artifact/VCEppdwfT7v32W4beUxL1v
(nine boards, `calibration-01…08` plus `05b`). The builder that drew them is outside the repo at
`~/.claude/projects/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/figma-mirror/tools/composer/build_calibration_page.py`.

- Board 1: the three "Calibrate…" rows, drawn as the app's menus are built today with one row added to each.
- Board 2: a symptom in the project chat. The agent explains, picks the test, then says in its own words that the
  current project will be saved and closed, that the test's settings are temporary, and that nothing is written
  until the person chooses. The reply choice is the confirmation; the calibration project then opens with the test
  already chosen, so board 4's question is skipped.
- Board 3: the one popup the menu rows show, in the Agent page's Confirmation dialog. It names the filament and
  printer, not a test, and carries the two facts: the project is saved and closed, the test's settings are temporary.
- Board 4: the calibration project. Its chat opens with a system line naming where it started from and for which
  filament and printer; the agent asks which test with reply chips; the person's chip reply; then the agent's word
  that the tower is on the plate, what to print and what to photograph. The pinned card is the Setup summary as
  `setup_record` fills it after generating.
- Board 5 and 5b: the photo comes back, the agent names the block and why, and proposes one write through the
  ordinary settings preview rows plus the preset it is saved as. 5b shows the card is one shape with slots (value,
  scope, base preset and printer, setting old → new, the word for what the person picks) and three instances.
- Board 6: the receipt with Undo. The agent tells the person the preset name to pick from now on; nothing switches.
- Board 7: the test reopened later warns that the steps are not in the file and offers to regenerate, as reply chips.
- Board 8: the test on Home as an ordinary project. Its card reads "Saved" like every card today (Home knows a
  closed project only by name, thumbnail and whether a print is running; `OrcaHomeBackend.cpp` ~line 202). The test
  is told apart by its project name.

The strings on the boards are illustrations; the agent writes its own. Keep the two facts of boards 2 and 3 verbatim
in meaning: the project closes, the test's edits are temporary.

## 5. The build: one tool, one skill, three rows, one carry-over, one optional seam

Do not build: a `calibration_list` tool (the tests are static knowledge; the workspace already reports printer,
filament and nozzle), per-test cards, a return hook, preset switching, or Bambu's automatic path. Correct the tool
guide (`agent-docs/jusprin/mcp-tool-extension-guide.md`, the `calibration` table around line 561): the
`calibration_generate` row says "onto a new plate", which fact 1 rules out, and `calibration_list` is dropped.

### 5.1 The tool: `calibration_generate`, and the carry-over it needs

One registered tool (`Agent/ToolRegistry.cpp`, handler in `ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp`, adapter work in
`Workspace/OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp`). Input: `test` (`temperature`, `flow`, `pressure_advance` for now) and the
test's parameters as Orca's dialogs take them (temperature and pressure advance: `start`, `end`, `step`; pressure
advance also `method` line/pattern/tower and `extruderType`; flow: `pass` 1 or 2 and `linear`). No project name: the
calibration project is already named when the tool runs. Output: the project's name, the plate and object ids, the
parameters as applied (Orca clamps and substitutes; return what it did) and the new `sessionId`, as `project_open`
returns one. Mark it in-app only until the MCP side is wanted.

The tool has one rule, whichever path reached it. First it makes sure the open project is a calibration project: if
it is not (the symptom path, where the agent calls from the person's own project), it releases the open project the
way `project_open` does (version saved, unsaved preset edits dropped) and creates the empty calibration project
through that same path, named "Calibration · <filament> · <printer>" and marked as a calibration project in the
fork's own project document (`Agent/ProjectPersistence`). Then it generates into it, in one call, with the
carry-over fact 9 showed is needed, all in fork-owned files:

1. `ProjectPersistence` gets a one-shot "the next project boundary continues this project". While it is armed,
   `adopt_current_project` keeps the current document (project id, chats, setup record) instead of calling
   `start_fresh_identity`; `ProjectAutosave::adopt_project` then returns early because the id is unchanged
   (`ProjectAutosave.cpp:459`), so version history continues in one store.
2. The shell's release hook (`ShellController.cpp:420`) does not save while the one-shot is armed: the same project

3. The tool arms the one-shot, calls the matching `Plater::calib_*` inside the adapter's existing tool-load scope
   (`ToolLoad`, as `open_project` uses it) so the generator's model load is not reported as a file the person
   opened, then calls `Plater::set_project_filename(<the project's name>)` before returning, ahead of the first
   autosave, and returns the new `sessionId`.
4. `AgentHost` drops a tool activity whose session is no longer current (`AgentHost.cpp:715`, "the last word of an
   action that replaced the project belongs to the project it closed"). A generate call that continued the project's
   identity is exempt: its result is recorded in the chat that asked, because that chat is still the project's. From
   the symptom path the person's own chat keeps the last word as `project_open` does today, and the calibration
   project's chat starts with the handover line of 5.3. State both in the tool's code where that rule lives.

### 5.2 The skill: `AgentUI/src/skills/calibration/SKILL.md`

Written 2026-10-22, revised 2026-10-23 after the Preferences window landed on jusprin-newui (641c17f13e,
80ed1692ff). Status: DECIDED by Kenneth on 2026-10-23 (Decisions 1, 2, 3 and 5 chosen in the session that wrote this;
Decision 4's rule was proposed to him in the same message and not objected to; Decision 6 was settled by the
code). Untracked on purpose; never commit it. For a cold reader: section 3 is the design; section 2 is why.

## 1. The problem

The Agent (the React chat in the WebView pane) answers nothing until a provider is set up: an API key or a
connected AI tool. Several places in JusPrin need the Agent, and each answers "none is set up" its own way.
Calibration ("Calibrate…" on the printer chip, the filament slot and the Home printer card) would add one more.
Kenneth called the pattern clunky and surprising, and objected to the first calibration proposal: "On the
homepage, most users don't have a workspace open. So we just randomly open a new workspace?"

## 2. What the app does today (jusprin-newui at ea9f684de0, read 2026-10-23)

A. **Print-issue bubble on the Prepare canvas** ("Ask AI", "Resolve with AI"; `Shell/ShellController.cpp`,
   `offer_agent_setup`, `open_agent_setup`). With no agent: OrcaSlicer's `MessageDialog` "The AI assistant isn't
   set up yet… Set up now / Not now". "Set up now" expands the docked Agent pane (switching Home to the
   workspace first, though the bubble only exists on the canvas) and swaps the pane's body for the provider
   chooser. When setup completes nothing continues; the person presses the bubble again. "Not now" changes
   nothing. Closing the chooser leaves the pane expanded on its "No agent connected" offer.

B. **The printer conversation panel** (`PrinterSetup/PrinterPanel.cpp`), opened by Home's "+ Add printer",
   "Printer settings…" and "Connect…", the project header's "Printer settings…" / "Add a printer…", and the
   filament slot's "Filament settings…". It covers the whole centre, Home included, with its own throwaway Agent
   runtime. With no agent its body is the offer ("No agent connected", "Set up the agent"); its header keeps
   "Back" and "Browse the full printer list" / "Open printer settings"; the add-printer form works without an
   agent. "Set up the agent" swaps the chooser into the panel; when setup completes
   (`set_setup_completed_listener`) the greeting continues in place and the docked pane is told to reload.

C. **The docked Agent pane's own entry** (`AgentUI/src/App.tsx`, `components/Setup.tsx`, `components/Panels.tsx`).
   An empty chat shows the offer; a chat with history shows a "Set up the agent" bar; the chat list says
   "Connect an Agent to continue this conversation". With no agent, setup swaps into the pane's body (chooser →
   API key or AI tool → connected). Since 641c17f13e, the same button with an agent already set up opens
   Preferences › Agent instead ("An agent that is set up is changed where every way of connecting is listed").

D. **Preferences › Agent, new** (`Preferences/PreferencesWindow.cpp`, `AgentUI/src/components/Preferences.tsx`,
   `AgentConnection.tsx`). JusPrin's own Preferences is a modal window over any screen: Home's gear, the
   project menu's "Preferences…", Cmd+, / Ctrl+,, Help › Check for Updates, OrcaSlicer's own menu items. Its
   Agent section draws the same rows setup draws (`ProviderKeys`: one row per provider with the key field,

   model, and the privacy line. It checks a key through the same setup service, so a key verified there is
   stored where setup stores it and records the same consent. When the window closes, the shell reloads the
   docked pane's agent if any `jusprin_agent` setting changed (`open_preferences`, `reload_agent_config`).

E. **Calibration, not built** (`calibration-handoff.md` 5.3; canvas page "Calibration · Printer & Filament",

So after the new commits there are still three first-time setup flows (A, B, C swap the chooser into a pane or

# Handoff: printer and filament calibration in JusPrin

Written 2026-10-21, revised 2026-10-22 for the one-popup flow and 2026-10-23 after the implementing agent's review,
for the agent who implements calibration. This document records the decisions Kenneth made, the facts verified in
OrcaSlicer's code (by reading and, for the flow, by running), the design on the canvas, and the smallest build that
satisfies both. Read `agent-docs/jusprin/README.md` and the documents it lists first; `fork-stewardship.md` governs
every line you change outside `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`. This file is untracked on purpose: never commit it.

## 1. What a calibration is, in one paragraph

A person has a symptom (stringing, under-extrusion, bulging corners) or just wants a filament dialled in. One popup
tells them their project will be saved and closed; then they are in an empty calibration project of its own, whose
agent has the context handed over, picks the test with them (asking only when the symptom did not decide it), and
generates OrcaSlicer's own test geometry into that project. The person prints it and sends a photo, the agent reads
the print and proposes a value, the person saves it as a new preset with one press, and the agent tells them the
preset's name to use from now on. The product definition's section 2.11 lists the eight agent steps; this handoff is
how they map onto code.

## 2. Decisions already made (Kenneth, 2026-10-21 to 2026-10-23)

1. A calibration is a project of its own, as long as the person is told what will happen before their project is
   closed. Not a plate in the current project (see fact 1 below for why that is impossible without rewriting Orca).
2. First batch: temperature tower, flow rate, pressure advance. Nothing else in this iteration.
3. The outcome of every test is a new preset: a named copy of the filament (or of the process or printer preset for
   the tests that write there). The app does not switch any project to it. The receipt names the preset and the
   agent tells the person to pick it from now on.
4. No remembered "return to the previous project". The test project is left through Home like any project.
5. No per-test UI. Adding a test must be a declaration plus skill text, not page code.
6. The physical-print ledger: "doesn't matter, whatever is the easiest". Leave it alone.
7. Entry points are hard-coded: a "Calibrate…" row in the project header's printer chip menu, in the filament slot
   menu, and in the Home printer card's kebab. A symptom typed in the project chat leads to the same flow.
8. The confirmation before a calibration is the Agent page's own Confirmation dialog, the one it draws for "Delete
   chat?": a web dialog, not Orca's `MessageDialog` and not a new native dialog (2026-10-21).
9. **One popup, then the calibration project** (2026-10-22, confirmed after the verification in fact 9). The popup
   names the filament and printer, not a test. After it, JusPrin creates and opens an empty, named calibration project
   and its chat, with the context handed over. The agent in that chat picks the test, asking "which test?" only when
   the handover does not decide it, and generates into that same project. The first implementation's flow (a popup
   about closing the project, then the agent asking which test, then a second project) is what this replaces.
10. Home's project cards do not change: no slice state, filament or calibration result on a card. The test is told
    apart by its project name (2026-10-22).
11. Choices under the agent's words are Chat/Reply Choice chips, never buttons. Buttons inside the thread belong only
    to cards drawn from tool results, the proposal and the receipt (2026-10-22).
12. **Saving the result is the person's press, applied by the app** (2026-10-22, decided with the implementing
    agent; recorded here 2026-10-23). The agent previews the write; the preview's result draws the proposal card of
    board 5; "Save preset" on that card makes the app apply the preview with its copy name. The agent's own apply
    of a calibration result is refused.
13. When the person is already on their own (non-stock) preset, the agent asks them whether to write the value into
    it or save a copy (2026-10-21). On a stock preset there is no question: a copy.
14. `calibration_generate` is offered over MCP as well as in-app (2026-10-21).
15. After a reload, option (a) of 5.4: the skill's regenerate offer, board 7 as drawn (2026-10-22). Not option (b).
16. **One name for the test everywhere** (2026-10-23): the project's, "Calibration · <filament> · <printer>" (or
    "Calibration · <printer>" from a Home card, decision 17). The chat's title, the pinned card's purpose, board 8's
    card and the receipt's wording all use it; the agent does not invent a second name.
17. **From a Home card the app knows the printer, not the spool** (2026-10-23). The popup names the printer only, the
    project is "Calibration · <printer>", the app selects that printer in the new project, and the handover tells
    the agent the filament is unknown, so the agent's first question offers the printer's loaded spools (or the
    installed filaments) as reply choices before asking which test. The app never guesses a filament: which spool is
    in the printer is a physical fact the person owns.
18. With no agent set up: the row's popup stays, with one added sentence and "Set up the agent…" as its primary
    action, which opens Preferences › Agent over the current screen (2026-10-23; details in 5.3 and in the untracked
    `agent-setup-flow-decisions.md`).

## 3. Facts verified in the code

Facts 1 to 8 were verified by reading on 2026-10-21; fact 9 by running code on 2026-10-22; fact 10 by reading on
2026-10-23.

1. **Every OrcaSlicer generator replaces the open project and edits project-wide presets.** `Plater::calib_pa`,
   `calib_temp`, `calib_flowrate`, `calib_max_vol_speed`, `calib_retraction`, `calib_VFA`, the input-shaping pair and
   `Calib_Cornering` (`src/slic3r/GUI/Plater.cpp` from about line 12677) each call `new_project()` and then write to
   `preset_bundle->prints/filaments/printers.get_edited_preset().config`. Plates have no presets of their own, so a
   test on a plate of an existing project would change every other plate. Do not try.
2. **The test's parameters are runtime-only.** The generator stores them on the current plate's `Print` with
   `set_calib_params` (`Print.hpp:1089`); `GCode.cpp` reads them per layer (temperature at line 4697). Nothing writes
   them to the 3MF, and loading a project resets the mode to none at `Plater.cpp:5891`. A saved temperature tower,
   reopened, slices as a plain tower at one temperature. The pressure-advance pattern is the exception: its per-layer
   commands go into the plate's custom G-code, which the 3MF does save. The PA pattern also hard-codes the first
   plate's origin (`Plater.cpp:12814`), which is right because the generator's `new_project()` selects plate 0.
3. **OrcaSlicer already treats one outcome as a new preset.** The Bambu wizard's save page writes flow results as a
   filament preset named "<filament> Flow Rate Calibrated" (`CalibrationWizardSavePage.cpp:37`). Its pressure-advance
   results go to the machine, not a preset. The SoftFever dialogs (`calib_dlg.cpp`) save nothing: the person types
   the value into a preset by hand.
4. **Saving a copy already exists and selects the copy.** `settings_apply_patch` with `persistAs` saves through
   Orca's own `Tab::save_preset` and asserts the copy is now selected
   (`Workspace/OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:3356-3369`); the result carries `saved_as`. A stock preset cannot be
   overwritten and the preview says so with `read_only_preset` and a suggested copy name (`check_persist`, line
   2941). Whether a process-scope copy works end to end is unverified; filament and printer are in use today.
5. **Which preset each result belongs to** (from `Preset.cpp`'s option lists): nozzle temperature, flow ratio,
   pressure advance, retraction length (as a filament override) and max volumetric speed are filament settings; VFA
   writes wall speeds in the process preset; cornering writes junction deviation (process) or jerk limits (printer);
   input shaping and Bambu's measured pressure advance live on the machine and produce no preset.
6. **The skill mechanism is ready.** `AgentUI/src/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` with a `description:` in its frontmatter is
   listed to the model and read on demand through the `skill_read` tool (`Agent/ToolRegistry.cpp:1209`,
   `AgentHost.cpp:2467`); a skill may also carry a `trigger:` the app fires on an event (`skillParser.ts`). Text limit
   16 KiB; one skill per directory; name equals directory name.
7. **The project-replacing path already exists.** The `project_open` tool saves the open project to its version
   history, drops unsaved preset edits, and calls `m_plater.new_project(true, true, name)` with confirmations skipped
   (`OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:2450-2467`, `ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp:1005`). Creating the calibration project
   takes this route, not a second one.
8. **The setup card is already data-driven.** `setup_record` (`ToolRegistry.cpp:1071`) titles the pinned card from a
   purpose and headline. A calibration project needs no new pinned card: the agent records the test as the purpose
   and the range as the headline.
9. **Generating into a project JusPrin already opened, verified by running** (report:
   `.claude/worktrees/kind-mestorf-a37ba6/calibration-generate-verification.md`, untracked; its probe, harness diff
   and log are in the shared notes folder `calibration-generate-probe/`). With the real adapter and shell, each of
   the three generators called in a fresh, empty, named JusPrin project:
   - shows no dialog, and builds a test identical to OrcaSlicer's own dialog path: same objects on plate 0, same
     per-object settings, same `calib_params` on the plate's print, same preset edits, and for the PA pattern the
     same per-layer custom G-code after `reslice()`;
   - but replaces the project all the same: the JusPrin project id, the workspace session and the chat document
     change, because `new_project()` gives the model a new auxiliary directory and `ProjectPersistence` treats that
     as a project boundary (`ProjectPersistence.cpp:181-185`, `start_fresh_identity`). An empty project that already
     holds a chat is saved by the shell's release hook and appears on Home as a separate project;
   - renames the project; `Plater::set_project_filename(name)` restores JusPrin's name, and the name survives a save
     only if it is set before the first autosave (`ProjectAutosave.cpp` fixed the name at the first version at lines
     515-519 when measured; the implementation branch has since changed those lines, and under the new flow the
     project is named before it is created, so the rename after generating matters for OrcaSlicer's title bar);
   - keeps an unsaved preset edit made in the empty project: it carries into the test, because JusPrin's release hook
     skips OrcaSlicer's keep-or-discard question (`Plater.cpp:12077`).
   So the one-popup flow needs the carry-over in 5.1 and no change to OrcaSlicer-owned code. The report recommends
   against a seam that lets a generator skip its own `new_project()`: three functions in `Plater.cpp`, and it would
   skip resets that keep the test identical to OrcaSlicer's.
10. **A project boundary also cancels the agent's turn.** Adopting a document at a boundary calls
    `ProjectPersistence::notify_document_replaced` (`ProjectPersistence.cpp:303-390`), and the host's handler
    (`AgentHost::on_document_replaced`, `AgentHost.cpp:793`) cancels the agent, resets the stream, clears every tool
    call and continuation, and drops live work. A generate call that kept the document but fired that notification
    would never deliver its result to the model, and it is the situation that crashed the app once (fixed in
    be98979009). The carry-over in 5.1 must suppress this notification as well as the session check.

## 4. The design

JusPrin v2 canvas, page "Calibration · Printer & Filament": https://claude.ai/artifact/VCEppdwfT7v32W4beUxL1v
(nine boards, `calibration-01…08` plus `05b`). The builder that drew them is outside the repo at
`~/.claude/projects/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/figma-mirror/tools/composer/build_calibration_page.py`.

- Board 1: the three "Calibrate…" rows, drawn as the app's menus are built today with one row added to each.
- Board 2: a symptom in the project chat. The agent explains, picks the test, then says in its own words that the
  current project will be saved and closed, that the test's settings are temporary, and that nothing is written
  until the person chooses. The reply choice is the confirmation; the calibration project then opens with the test
  already chosen, so board 4's question is skipped.
- Board 3: the one popup the menu rows show, in the Agent page's Confirmation dialog, in two states. With an agent: it
  names the filament and printer, not a test, carries the two facts (the project is saved and closed, the test's
  settings are temporary), and its primary action is "Start". With no agent: the same dialog with one added
  sentence and "Set up the agent…" as its primary action.
- Board 4: the calibration project. Its chat, titled with the project's name, opens with a system line naming where
  it started from and for which filament and printer; the agent asks which test with reply chips; the person's chip
  reply; then the agent's word that the tower is on the plate, what to print and what to photograph. The pinned
  card is the Setup summary as `setup_record` fills it after generating.
- Board 5 and 5b: the photo comes back, the agent names the block and why, and the preview's result draws the
  proposal card: the ordinary settings preview rows plus the preset it is saved as, with "Save preset", which the app
  applies on the press. 5b shows the card is one shape with slots (value, scope, base preset and printer, setting
  old → new, the word for what the person picks) and three instances.
- Board 6: the receipt with Undo. The agent tells the person the preset name to pick from now on; nothing switches.
- Board 7: the test reopened later warns that the steps are not in the file and offers to regenerate, as reply chips.
- Board 8: the test on Home as an ordinary project named "Calibration · Gray PETG · Prusa MK4". Its card reads
  "Saved" like every card today (Home knows a closed project only by name, thumbnail and whether a print is
  running; `OrcaHomeBackend.cpp` ~line 202). The test is told apart by its project name.

The strings on the boards are illustrations; the agent writes its own. Keep the two facts of boards 2 and 3 verbatim
in meaning: the project closes, the test's edits are temporary.

## 5. The build: one tool, one skill, three rows, one carry-over

Do not build: a `calibration_list` tool (the tests are static knowledge; the workspace already reports printer,
filament and nozzle), per-test cards, a return hook, preset switching, Bambu's automatic path, or any seam in
OrcaSlicer-owned code for the generators. Correct the tool guide (`agent-docs/jusprin/mcp-tool-extension-guide.md`,

### 5.1 The tool: `calibration_generate`, and the carry-over it needs

`Workspace/OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp`), offered in-app and over MCP (decision 14). Input: `test` (`temperature`,
`flow`, `pressure_advance` for now), the test's parameters as Orca's dialogs take them (temperature and pressure
advance: `start`, `end`, `step`; pressure advance also `method` line/pattern/tower and `extruderType`; flow: `pass`
1 or 2 and `linear`), and an optional `symptom`, the person's words that led here, which the handover line repeats.
No project name: the app names the calibration project. Output: the project's name, the plate and object ids, the
parameters as applied (Orca clamps and substitutes; return what it did) and the new `sessionId`, as `project_open`
returns one.

The tool has one rule, whichever path reached it. First it makes sure the open project is a calibration project: if
it is not (the symptom path, where the agent calls from the person's own project), it releases the open project the
way `project_open` does (version saved, unsaved preset edits dropped) and creates the empty calibration project
through that same path, named "Calibration · <filament> · <printer>" and marked as a calibration project in the
fork's own project document (`Agent/ProjectPersistence`). Then it generates into it, in one call, with the
carry-over facts 9 and 10 showed is needed, all in fork-owned files:

1. `ProjectPersistence` gets a one-shot "the next project boundary continues this project". While it is armed,
   `adopt_current_project` keeps the current document (project id, chats, setup record) instead of calling
   `start_fresh_identity`, and does not call `notify_document_replaced` (fact 10), so the agent's turn, its tool
   calls and its continuations survive the boundary. `ProjectAutosave::adopt_project` then returns early because
   the id is unchanged (`ProjectAutosave.cpp:459`), so version history continues in one store.
2. The shell's release hook (`ShellController.cpp:420`) does not save while the one-shot is armed: the same project
   continues, so no separate empty project reaches Home. (The implementation branch already has this skip.)
3. The tool arms the one-shot, calls the matching `Plater::calib_*` inside the adapter's existing tool-load scope
   (`ToolLoad`, as `open_project` uses it) so the generator's model load is not reported as a file the person
   opened, then calls OrcaSlicer's existing public `Plater::set_project_filename(<the project's name>)` before
   returning, ahead of the first autosave, and returns the new `sessionId`. No forwarder added to `Plater`.
4. Which chat records the result. `AgentHost` drops a tool activity whose session is no longer current
   (`AgentHost.cpp:715`, "the last word of an action that replaced the project belongs to the project it closed").
   A tool call belongs to one chat. In a calibration project the one-shot keeps the document, so the session check
   must treat the continued project as current and the result lands in the chat that asked. From the symptom path
   the result stays in the person's own chat, as `project_open`'s does today, and the calibration project's chat
   opens with the handover line of 5.3 and nothing else. State both rules in the tool's code where that check lives.

### 5.2 The skill: `AgentUI/src/skills/calibration/SKILL.md`

at the material or when the person asks to calibrate, and `trigger: calibration_started`, which the app fires for the

1. When a test is justified, and which symptoms point to which test (stringing and hairs: temperature first,
   retraction second; under-extrusion, gaps, bulging corners or top surface: flow; corner bulges and gap at seams at
   speed: pressure advance). Say when drying the spool or checking the nozzle comes first.
2. In a calibration project whose handover names no filament (a Home card): first ask which spool, offering the
   printer's loaded spools, or the installed filaments, as reply choices; never assume one. Then, when the handover
   names no test: ask which test, as reply choices, with one line each on what it shows and the order to take them

   it, do not ask.
3. From the person's own project (the symptom path): say the two facts (project saved and closed; temporary
   settings) and get a reply before calling `calibration_generate`, passing the person's words as `symptom`. In a

   generator's business.

   read the print; which setting the result writes and in which preset scope.
6. After generating: call `setup_record` with the project's name as the purpose and the range as the headline, then
